title: Schema Drift Penalty & Automatic Recovery Suite for FP8/INT8 Function-Call Outputs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add a regression test harness and CI pipeline that quantifies structured-output (function-call/JSON) schema conformance under FP8/INT8 profiles, assigns a per-config "penalty" score for nonconformance, and validates automatic recovery policies that degrade to safer model variants or higher-precision execution when penalties exceed thresholds.
background: Recent calibration runs and customer reports show intermittent schema drift for function-call outputs when models are served in low-precision modes. Existing unit schema checks catch obvious failures but lack a continuous penalty signal and an automated mitigation test that simulates production routing and fallbacks. We need an observability-and-test layer that connects calibration artifacts with runtime recovery behavior.
proposed_solution: Build a 'schema-penalty' metric that aggregates schema errors (missing required fields, type mismatches, enum violations, extra unknown props) weighted by severity and token position. Integrate the metric into the calibration workflow so that FP8/INT8 profiles are annotated with expected penalty ranges. Extend CI to run end-to-end scenarios that exercise the recovery policy: fallback to INT16/FP16 execution, switch to quantization 'safe' model variant, or route to a validation proxy that repairs minor structure issues. Add dashboards and per-profile alerts.
calibration_steps: Run batch calibration suite with current FP8/INT8 profiles on the curated function-call prompt corpus (2000 prompts)
Collect structured-output traces including token-by-token emissions, KV cache metadata, and JSON parse attempts
Compute schema-penalty per trace and aggregate per-profile statistics (median, 95th percentile)
Flag profiles where 95th percentile penalty > threshold and add to 'review' bucket
For flagged profiles, run focused reruns with adjusted calibration (scale tweaks, per-layer quant tables) and recompute penalties
test_plan: End-to-end CI job 'schema-penalty-e2e' that deploys model variant into test runtime with simulated request load (small batches + single shot)
Inject edge-case prompts that historically trigger malformed function calls (deeply nested objects, long arrays, unicode escapes)
Assert penalty metrics and trace logs are produced and ingested into the dashboard
Trigger recovery policy in test harness and confirm fallback route returned identical schema-conformant output or graceful error code
Record and publish per-run artifacts: model config, quant-profile, penalty histogram, failing traces
acceptance_criteria: CI job completes reliably with <2% flakiness over 10 runs
Schema-penalty metric is computed and stored for each quantization profile in the calibration artifacts
Automatic recovery policy triggers in simulated overload/failure runs and returns a schema-conformant response in >= 99% of triggered cases
Dashboard page 'Quantization -> Schema Penalty' exists and exposes per-profile 50/95/99 percentiles and trend lines
Playbook entry and runbook created describing thresholds, owner, and manual escalation steps

progress_updates: 2026-02-20: Spike complete, prototype penalty scorer implemented against small corpus. Observed concentrated failures around long arrays and enum casing (Aisha).

2026-02-28: First CI runs flaky (approx 12%) due to nondeterministic RNG in synthetic prompt generator; added seed control and reduced flakiness to ~3% (Aisha).

2026-03-03: Recovery simulator implemented for fallback to FP16 execution; found a small mismatch where KV cache warmup differs between variants, causing transient malformed outputs — tracking as follow-up task.
